sentences.text: Okay, so here's the thing nobody tells you about ice. It should sink, and it doesn't.
Sunlight is every colour at once, so why is the only one you ever see overhead blue?
A sealed jar of honey will outlive everyone who argues about it.
There are more ways to shuffle a deck of cards than there are seconds since the big bang.
Water reaches its densest point at three point nine eight degrees, not at zero.
Put any other cheese in a hot pan and it melts. Halloumi just sits there and squeaks.

paragraphs.text: Almost everything shrinks when it freezes. Water does the exact opposite, and that one quirk is why anything survives a winter. Ice floats, so a lake freezes from the top down instead of the bottom up, and the fish underneath carry on as though nothing has happened.

Most things spoil because something living got into them, and living things need water. Take the water out and the problem largely goes with it. A sealed jar on a shelf offers a microbe nothing at all to drink. Salt does it, sugar does it, and smoke, acid and cold all help in their own fashion.
